tier2.summary:
INCOMPLETE
  ✗ Cold limit=10 on coding-hermes and fleet-quality answers in under 500ms with no rows lost, proven by a committed benchmark script; the list path no longer depends on total file count; tests pass.: The criterion has four conjunctive parts; two fail decisively. (A) '<500ms proven by a committed benchmark script' — scripts/perf/perf001-list-latency.mjs IS committed (git ls-files confirms) and does sample coding-hermes + fleet-quality at limit=10, but it contains ZERO occurrences of '500' (grep -c '500' -> 0): it never asserts a latency threshold, only throwing on HTTP error or items.length>10, so it cannot prove the target. No committed benchmark RESULT artifact exists (git ls-files | grep perf001 -> only the script plus two test files). The repo's own committed board record contradicts the claim: .coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl PERF-DUCKBRAIN-001 foreman_note states 'target (cold <500ms) NOT met yet, production NOT compacted', with measured production coding-hermes limit=10 at 1.42/1.88/2.00s and fleet-quality 13.26s cold / 1.82s warm; board status is still 'pending', worker_status 'pending', commit_hash null. (B) 'the list path no longer depends on total file count' — FAIL: the new runBoundedRead() at src/duckdb/queries.ts:801-812 still executes `FROM read_json([${fileList}], ...)` over the FULL file list (line 810), and collectJsonlFiles() (queries.ts:151) still readdir's every .jsonl in every partition. No index/mtime/newest-N/segment-ordering mechanism exists (grep for mtime|newest-N|bounded index|segment ordering in queries.ts -> no matches). Only the dedup SORT is bounded (page CTE LIMIT ${window}, window = limit+50, cap 100_000); the per-file ingest/metadata cost the task itself names as the cause ('the cause is FILE COUNT (20k-29k jsonl files per namespace)') is untouched, so latency still scales with file count. (C) 'no rows lost' — partially supported: src/duckdb/queries-plainlist-bounded-perf001.test.ts proves byte-equivalence of page+total vs queryMemoriesWithTotalFused across duplicate ids, tombstones, boundary straddles, offsets and limit=0, and total == brute-force deduped count, but only on tiny synthetic fixtures. (D) 'tests pass' — PASS, actual output: `npx vitest run src/duckdb/queries-plainlist-bounded-perf001.test.ts` exit 0, 'Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 4 passed (4)'; `npx vitest run src/duckdb/` exit 0, 'Test Files 13 passed (13) / Tests 128 passed (128)'; `npx vitest run src/http/ src/keys/` exit 0, 'Test Files 66 passed (66) / Tests 481 passed (481)'; `npx vitest run src/mcp/ src/search/` exit 0, 'Test Files 31 passed (31) / Tests 300 passed (300)'. The full `npx vitest run` exceeded the 30s tool cap, so the relevant subsets were run instead. Net: the bounded top-k is a real optimization and its tests are green, but the <500ms target is unproven and self-contradicted by the repo's own record, and the file-count dependency is not removed.
The bounded top-k change and its tests are green, but the <500ms cold-latency target is neither asserted by the committed benchmark nor met (the repo's own board note says 'NOT met yet'), and the list path still read_json's every file so latency still scales with file count.
